messages:
nina: New hire report: redwoodctl login --local-serve never returned the callback. Browser opened to localhost:8087 but CLI stayed "Waiting for auth callback..." and then timed out. macOS Ventura.

own: Any chance there are two redwoodctl binaries on PATH? `which -a redwoodctl` can show. We had a pkg installer and a manual unzip collision recently.

nina: Yup: old copy in /usr/local/bin and new pkg in /opt/redwood/bin. Removed old one, re-ran login, saw macOS firewall popup and then CLI errored: "listen EACCES 0.0.0.0:8087". Allowing incoming connections fixed it.

lee: Issues to file: (1) CLI should catch EACCES and print a macOS hint about Firewall and moved binaries; (2) pkg/msi postinstall should scan PATH and warn about leftover redwoodctl executables; (3) Quickstart should show device-code fallback env var.

owen: For headless/CI folks use REDWOODCTL_DEVICE_CODE=1 or REDWOODCTL_NO_BROWSER=1; we need that in docs. Also propose CLI interactive fallback: after a bind error prompt "Press Enter to fall back to device-code flow".

nina: One more: sample-app env uses REDWOOD_API_URL in docs but local-serve expects REDWOODCTL_API_URL. Tiny mismatch that trips onboarding. Can we accept REDWOOD_API_URL as alias?

lee: Low-risk: add alias and update Quickstart. I'll take the CLI error message and alias change. Owen, can you open the installer issue for PATH-scan and a docs PR for device-code examples?

owen: On it. Filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/1560

bot-ci: CI: pre-release redwoodctl-0.9.2-beta built. artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/4001

nina: Thanks all. After removing the old binary and allowing firewall the login flow worked. The device-code tip helped others on WSL too.
